text:
ConocoPhillips fell 0.83% today, continuing a decline that has knocked the stock down $5.37 over the past week. The immediate driver appears to be softening oil prices: US crude dropped to $83.90 per barrel, down from the mid-$130s range when the stock was at $134, suggesting weaker energy demand or supply concerns easing. This follows a broader retreat after a brief rally earlier in the month.

The backdrop for this weakness is a shift in geopolitical risk perception around the Strait of Hormuz—a critical chokepoint for global oil. While an Iran-US conflict has dragged on longer than expected, recent diplomatic moves (Qatar's mediation, Iran's signals about returning to talks) appear to have reduced immediate fears of a major supply disruption. That lowered tension likely contributed to oil prices easing off their highs, even as Europe's gas shortage and lingering Middle East uncertainty keep energy costs elevated enough to support prices above $80.
